record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Is every Polish countable dense homogeneous space omega-CDH, meaning that any two countable indexed families of pairwise disjoint countable dense sets can be matched coordinatewise by a self-homeomorphism?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Is every Polish CDH space ω-CDH?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A separable metrizable space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D, E \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h : X \to X$ with $h(D) = E$. A Polish space is a separable, completely metrizable topological space.

Say that $X$ is $\omega$-CDH if for any two sequences $(D_n)_{n \in \omega}$ and $(E_n)_{n \in \omega}$ of countable dense subsets of $X$ such that the $D_n$ are pairwise disjoint and the $E_n$ are pairwise disjoint, there exists a single homeomorphism $h : X \to X$ with $h(D_n) = E_n$ for every $n \in \omega$.

Question: Is every Polish CDH space $\omega$-CDH?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a survey on countable dense homogeneity. Web searches did not surface any subsequent paper announcing a solution; recent works (2024–2025) on CDH continue to cite it among open problems, so it appears still open.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as an open problem in a survey on CDH.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity in large products of Polish spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on CDH in Polish spaces continues to investigate ω-CDH and related questions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to discuss the ω-CDH property without announcing a resolution to whether every Polish CDH space is ω-CDH.
